title: Atomic Design Transformer: Scaffold-Conditioned 3D Molecule Generation via xTB-Reward Reinforcement Learning
figure: First transformer for scaffold-conditioned 3D molecule generation via autoregressive placement.
abstract: The Atomic Design Transformer (ADT) is introduced for 3D molecule generation, placing atoms autoregressively while ensuring SE(3) invariance through tokenization. The model benchmarks scaffold-conditioned generation across drug-like scaffolds, achieving high topology-preservation rates and valid-molecule yields. title: TanGO: Training-Free 3D Editing via Tangent-Space Guidance and Optimization
figure: First training-free 3D editing framework that enables adaptive per-token steering via tangent-space guidance.
abstract: TanGO is a training-free framework for 3D editing that improves upon existing generative models by allowing adaptive control of tokens in tangent space, reducing artifacts and enhancing performance in 3D editing tasks. The method employs a one-step optimal control rule to manage token control signals effectively.

title: Nexus: Native Mesh Generation with Diffusion
figure: First holistic mesh generation method via decoupled vertex and topology generation using diffusion.
abstract: Nexus introduces a diffusion method for generating high-quality triangle meshes by decoupling vertex and topology generation. It utilizes a coarse-to-fine approach for vertex generation and a novel Spacetime Interval for efficient topology modeling. The method outperforms existing autoregressive and two-stage baselines, as confirmed by user studies.

title: DiffGI: Differentiable Geometry Images for High-Fidelity Thin-Shell 3D Generation
figure: First differentiable geometry image framework for high-fidelity thin-shell 3D generation via VAE.
abstract: DiffGI introduces a novel end-to-end framework for 3D-to-2D mapping that integrates surface representation and geometric optimization. It replaces binary occupancy maps with a continuous 2D TSDF, eliminating artifacts and enabling gradient propagation for training. title: Compos3D: Interactive Part-Based Composition for Creative Control in Generative 3D Models
figure: First interactive part-based composition system for generative 3D models via remixing.
abstract: Compos3D introduces a compositional workflow for generative 3D modeling, allowing users to generate multiple candidates from prompts, select parts of interest, and assemble them into a refined model. This approach enhances creative control and aligns better with user intent compared to traditional regeneration workflows, as shown in a user study.

title: ABot-3DWorld 0: A Universal World Model to Explore Any 3D Space
figure: First universal multimodal 3D world model that generates explorable 3D spaces from text, image, and video inputs.
abstract: ABot-3DWorld 0 is a universal multimodal 3D world model that transforms text, image, and video inputs into high-fidelity, explorable 3D worlds. It utilizes a Spatial Generative Primitive for efficient 3D space description and includes a pipeline for generating panoramic videos and photorealistic 3D Gaussian Splatting worlds, achieving state-of-the-art results in scene fidelity.

title: LATO.2: Factorized 3D Mesh Generation with Vertex and Topology Flow
figure: First factorized flow matching framework for topology-aware mesh generation.
abstract: LATO.2 introduces a factorized flow matching framework for generating 3D meshes, separating vertex and connectivity flows to improve geometric fidelity and connectivity quality. This approach allows for part-wise generation and topology-adaptive editing, resulting in higher-resolution meshes compared to traditional methods.

title: Grassmannian Splatting I: Moving rank-2 Spacetime Surfels for Dynamic Scene Rendering
figure: First dynamic scene representation using Grassmannian splatting for rendering via Gaussian primitives.
abstract: Grassmannian splatting introduces a novel dynamic scene representation using Gaussians on 3-planes in spacetime. It allows for efficient rendering of rank-2 surfels, achieving faster training times compared to existing methods while maintaining high quality. The approach integrates static and dynamic behaviors seamlessly, making it suitable for real-time applications.
